·
Transfusion safe only if recipient won’t produce
Ab against donor Ag

·
Non-self anti-A, Anti-B developed in first
  year of life if type O blood (diet exposure)

·
Note no plasma in donor packed RBCs, hence
  donor’s antibodies unimportant

·
Many types (A, a, B, b etc); D most important

·
Non-self Anti-RhD only developed after
  exposure to RhD+ blood (no diet exposure)

·
Incompatibility -> extravascular haemolysis
  (not quite as bad)

·
Important to avoid sensitization in females of
  childbearing potential:
·
First time: Rh- mother,

·
First time: Rh- mother, Rh+ neonate ->
  sensitization

·
Second time: Rh+ neonate, maternal Anti-RhD
  IgG causes hydrops foetalis, haemolytic Dx of newbor

·
RBCs: “O Ag” but no A, B or RhD Ag

·
Plasma has anti-A, anti-B, +/- anti-RhD but
  these are washed from RBC unit

·
Safe for A,B,O whether D+ or D-

·
Useful in emergency when no time for
  crossmatch
